ingredients.item: Boneless white fish fillets (cod or tilapia)

instructions: Start the rice first. Rinse 1 1/2 cups basmati rice and cook it the way you usually do.
Pat the fish dry and cut it into 8 even pieces. Rub them with 1 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the turmeric, and let them sit while you make the paste.

Cut the stem off 1 green chili and slice the other 2 thinly for the table. Put the 4 tbsp mustard seeds, the coconut, the whole chili, 1/2 tsp of the salt, the remaining 1/2 tsp turmeric and 3 tbsp cold water into a blender.
Blend to a thick, rough paste, about 1 minute. That should be about 3/4 cup. Stir in 2 tbsp of the mustard oil.
Add the fish to the paste and turn each piece until it's coated. Let it sit for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, tear off 8 squares of foil, each about 10 inches. Put a piece of fish on each square, spoon the paste left in the bowl over the top and drizzle with a few drops of the last 1 tbsp mustard oil.
Fold each square over the fish and crimp the edges tight so nothing leaks. You'll have 8 packets.
Set a large skillet over medium-low heat. Lay the packets in a single layer, cover the pan and cook for 8 minutes. Work in two batches if they don't fit.
Flip the packets, cover and cook the other side for 8 minutes. Stand back a little when you open the foil, the steam is hot.

You're cooking the fish to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one piece there. No thermometer? Open a packet and press the fish with a fork. It's done when it flakes easily and is opaque all the way through.
Open the packets onto a platter and spoon the juices and paste over the fish. Taste a little of the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice. Set the sliced green chilies on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: No version of this dish has a rating anywhere, so it's a fallback and no trusted cook has it. Yummraj leads (mustard, coconut, turmeric and green chili, with foil allowed in place of banana leaf). Indrani's and Coffee and Crumpets agree on a mustard seed paste and mustard oil, and differ on adding poppy seeds or tomato and on steaming versus pan or oven. Foil replaces banana leaf and the packets cook on a covered skillet. One green chili goes in the paste and the rest go on the table.
